 Live Updates Updated Mon, Nov 9 2026 10:33 PM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email S&P 500 futures are little changed as traders brace for crucial consumer inflation report: Live updates
 Lee Ying Shan Ananya Chetia Traders work on the floor of the American Stock Exchange (AMEX) at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US, on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images U.S. stock futures largely traded near the flatline Monday night as traders awaited a pivotal consumer inflation report.
 S&P 500 futures were marginally higher, while futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average were up just 18 points. Nasdaq-100 futures added 0.2%. 
 In Asia, South Korea's Kospi surged 4.3% Tuesday. Japan's  Nikkei 225 added 2.89%, while Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 1.27%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index rose 0.42% and mainland's CSI 300 added 0.26%.
 During the regular U.S. trading day, the Dow Industrials gained 1,104 points, or 2.2%, while the S&P 500 popped about 2.4%. The Nasdaq Composite rose 2.7%. Monday's rally came after a rocky week for markets, in which traders grew concerned of an impending slowdown in data center buildouts after Democrats posted big victories in the midterm elections.
 While the tech sector rebounded in Monday's regular trading, Nvidia sat out the rally. 
 Shares of the chipmaker slid 4% after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted on Sunday to having an affair with a woman who U.S. intelligence officials, according to The New York Times, say is a spy for China's Ministry of State Security. The company's board of directors also launched an independent internal investigation , pointing to recent reporting that Huang "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort."
 Oil prices also fell on Monday, lending the market support. The U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures settled down more than 4%, while Brent crude futures slid more than 5%. 
 Investors are awaiting the October consumer price index report due on Tuesday. Economists polled by Dow Jones see headline CPI growing at a rate of 0.3% and core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy costs, rising 0.2% from the prior month. 
 This would mark a deceleration from September's readings, when headline CPI grew 0.6% and core CPI advanced 0.3%.
 "We think the slowdown in core CPI will stem from a reversion of shelter prices, primarily owners' equivalent rents and lodging away from home. Similarly, the stabilization in diesel prices should help to quell price pressures in energy-intensive goods," wrote Christopher Hodge, chief economist of the U.S. at Natixis CIB Americas. 
 Annual figures will not be provided for Tuesday's report because of the 2025 government shutdown. At that time, the Bureau of Labor Statistics was unable to collect some data which means there isn't a comparable figure for the index. 
 1 Hour Ago China imports top estimates in October as surplus narrows — but crosses $1 trillion in 10 months
 China's exports and imports surged more than expected in October, according to official data released Tuesday, while its surplus shrank sharply, undershooting estimates.
 Goods exports soared by 35.2% last month from a year earlier, exceeding expectations for a 33.5% jump in a Reuters poll but slowing from the 36.3% growth in September.
 Imports climbed by 41.6% last month, customs data showed, jumping from 31% in September and sharply beating Reuters-polled analysts' estimates of a 32% rise.
 The trade surplus dropped to $105.3 billion in October, the lowest level since April, according to LSEG data, with year-to-date figure at $1.04 trillion, compared to a record $1.2 trillion for the full year 2025. Calls from trading partners have grown louder for Beijing to boost domestic demand and balance its economy.
 — Anniek Bao 
Correction: This post has been updated to reflect that the data was released on Tuesday. 
 4 Hours Ago South Korea's stock exchange temporary halts buy-side trading on Kospi as index surges
 The Korea Exchange activated buy-side trading curbs on both benchmark Kospi on Tuesday as the index surged over 5%.
 The exchange triggered a "sidecar" mechanism, suspending program buying for five minutes. The mechanism is activated when the Kospi 200 futures index gains 5% or more for at least one minute.
 The Korean index, dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix, has been seeing heightened volatility as AI plays have come under increased investor scrutiny.
 —Lee Ying Shan 
 4 Hours Ago South Korea's Kospi jumps 5% as Asia markets open higher
 Asia-Pacific markets opened higher on Tuesday, as investors bought the dip in tech stocks.
 South Korea's Kospi surged 5.09%, while the small-cap, tech-heavy Kosdaq Index popped over 4.73%.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225 added 2.78%, while the Topix rose 1.77%. 
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was up 1.19%.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 5 Hours Ago Chicago Fed's Goolsbee expresses concern on inflation ahead of CPI report
 Ahead of the consumer price index reading set to roll out Tuesday morning, Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee flagged inflation fears. 
 "We go around, we talk to people everywhere in this district, all we hear about is affordability on the business side, the cost,"  said he said at a Monday event in his home district. "So we've got to come to terms with this cost-side and inflation-side failure."
 Goolsbee added the build-out related to artificial intelligence is also heightening the concerns. 
 "Now this stuff with the AI data center build-out is, to my eyes, starting to look more just like old-fashioned demand overheating," he said.
 Read more from CNBC's Jeff Cox on what to expect in the CPI report out Tuesday .
 — Ananya Chetia 
 5 Hours Ago Trump says Jensen Huang told him he didn't know his affair partner 'was a spy'
 President Donald Trump said Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang denied to him on Monday that he knew the woman he had an extramarital affair with "was a spy" for China. 
 "I asked him that question: 'Did you have any idea that she was a spy?' He said, 'I had no idea that she was a spy,'" Trump told reporters at the White House.
 The president's comments come after Huang admitted on Sunday that he had an extramarital affair . The Nvidia board then announced it would initiate an investigation following recent reporting that Huang had been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort." 
 The New York Times reported on Oct 29 that Alice Huang, who had developed a close relationship with the Nvidia executive, had come under scrutiny by U.S. spy agencies and "American officials had concluded that she was a Chinese intelligence asset, funneling information to Beijing." 
 Read more about from CNBC's Dan Mangan on Trump's comments on Jensen Huang here .
 — Ananya Chetia 
 5 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets set to track Wall Street rally as oil drops, tech rebounds
 Asia-Pacific markets were set to rise on Tuesday, tracking gains on Wall Street overnight as a sharp decline in oil prices and a rebound in technology stocks lifted investor sentiment.
 Futures for Japan's  Nikkei 225  in Chicago were at 61,035 while in Osaka they were last at 60,930, compared with the index's previous close of 58,775.5.
 Futures for Hong Kong's Hang Seng index last traded at 24,506 compared with the index's last close of 24,448.73.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was up 0.79% in early trade.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 5 Hours Ago Stock futures were flat on Monday.
 Stock futures traded near the flatline on Monday. 
 S&P 500 futures gained just 0.07%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures rose 12 points, or 0.02%. Nasdaq-100 futures were up 0.19%.
 — Ananya Chetia
